It was on their invitation that the Lowenstein's visited St. Ives, probably in the spring of 1942, and were introduced to the town's artistic community including Ben Nicholson and Barbara Hepworth. provenance: With Stone Gallery, Newcastle, where acquired by the family of the present owner. Private Collection, U.K. The present and following two lots were acquired by the late father of the present owner during the mid to late 1960s, while he was a young dentist living and working in the North-East of England. Having studied in both Durham and Newcastle upon Tyne before joining a dental practice in Darlington, he developed an early appreciation for Northern art and for artists whose work captured the character, humour and humanity of everyday industrial life. A regular visitor to the Stone Gallery in Newcastle, the dentist met L.S. Lowry and acquired these three Lowry works, together with paintings by important Northern artists including Norman Cornish and Sheila Fell (to be offered in forthcoming Bonhams auctions in July and September), both of whom were then emerging talents and are now recognised as major figures in twentieth-century British art. Among the Lowry works was Sea Tests (lot 41), a pencil work that became especially treasured within the family. The dentist's eldest daughter recalls hours spent carefully copying the picture, and in 1975 her father presented the child's drawing to Lowry - a memory he always valued greatly. The collection also includes Apple Annie (lot 42), one of Lowry's memorable character studies. Family conversations over the years recalled the story that Annie was a local working girl who discreetly kept her telephone number hidden in a nearby telephone box, adding another layer of humour and humanity to Lowry's fascination with ordinary Northern lives and personalities.
